sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第035卷

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 35.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 35.

sentences.zh: 【漢紀二十七】起屠維協洽，盡玄黓閹茂，凡四年。

translations.literal: [Han Annals 27] From Tuwie Xieqia through Xuanmo Yanmao; four years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Han Annals 27] From Tuwie Xieqia through Xuanmo Yanmao—four years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛丑朔，詔將軍、中二千石舉明習兵法者各一人，因就拜孔鄉侯傅晏為大司馬、衛將軍，陽安侯丁明為大司馬、票騎將軍。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the xinchou new moon, an edict ordered generals and rank-2000-shi to each recommend one clearly skilled in military law; thereupon on the spot Marquis of Kongxiang Fu Yan was appointed Grand Marshal and Defender General, and Marquis of Yang'an Ding Ming Grand Marshal and Rapid Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the xinchou new moon, an edict ordered generals and rank-2000-shi officials each to recommend one man clearly versed in military law; thereupon Marquis of Kongxiang Fu Yan was appointed on the spot as Grand Marshal and Defender General, and Marquis of Yang'an Ding Ming as Grand Marshal and Rapid Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 是日，日有食之。

translations.literal: That day, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: That day there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 上詔公卿大夫悉心陳過失；

translations.literal: The emperor edicted dukes, ministers, and grandees to exhaust their hearts in stating faults;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor edicted the dukes, ministers, and grandees to lay out faults with full candor;

sentences.zh: 又令舉賢良方正能直言者各一人。

translations.literal: He also ordered that one worthy and upright man able to speak frankly be recommended from each.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered that one worthy and upright man able to speak frankly be recommended from each district.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 丞相嘉奏封事曰：「孝元皇帝奉承大業，溫恭少欲，都內錢四十萬萬。

translations.literal: Chancellor Jia submitted a sealed memorial, saying: "Emperor Yuan received the great enterprise, warm and respectful, few in desires; capital cash forty myriads of myriads.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Wang Jia submitted a sealed memorial: "Emperor Yuan received the great enterprise—warm, respectful, and sparing in desire—and there were four hundred million cash coins within the capital.

sentences.zh: 嘗幸上林，後宮馮貴人從臨獸圈，猛獸驚出，貴人前當之，元帝嘉美其義，賜錢五萬。

translations.literal: Once he visited Shanglin; Palace Lady Feng of the rear apartments followed him to the beast pens; a fierce beast startled out; the lady stepped before it to block; Emperor Yuan praised her righteousness and granted fifty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Once he visited Shanglin Park; Palace Lady Feng of the rear apartments followed him to the beast pens, a fierce beast bolted out, and the lady stepped before him to shield him. Emperor Yuan praised her righteousness and granted her fifty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 掖庭見親，有加賞賜，屬其人勿眾謝。

translations.literal: When the palace women received audiences, if there were added rewards, he charged the person not to thank him before the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: When palace women received audiences and were given added rewards, he charged them not to thank him publicly before the multitude.

sentences.zh: 示平惡偏，重失人心，賞賜節約。

translations.literal: He showed fairness and hated partiality, weighted not losing people's hearts, and was sparing in rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He showed fairness and hated partiality, prized not losing the people's hearts, and was sparing in rewards.

sentences.zh: 是時外戚貲千萬者少耳，故少府、水衡見錢多也。

translations.literal: At that time among affinal kin those with wealth of ten million were few, hence the Privy Treasurer and Palace Parks had much visible cash.
translations.idiomatic: At that time few affinal kin held wealth of ten million, and so the Privy Treasurer and Palace Parks offices had abundant cash on hand.

sentences.zh: 雖遭初元、永光凶年饑饉，加以西羌之變，外奉師旅，內振貧民，終無傾危之憂，以府臧內充實也。

translations.literal: Though they met the Chuyuan and Yongguang evil years of famine, plus the Western Qiang disturbance, outwardly supporting armies, inwardly reviving the poor—in the end no fear of toppling peril, because the treasury stores within were full.
translations.idiomatic: Though the realm suffered famine in the Chuyuan and Yongguang years and the Western Qiang rose in revolt, supporting armies abroad while reviving the poor at home, there was never fear of collapse—because the treasury within was full.

sentences.zh: 孝成皇帝時，諫臣多言燕出之害，及女寵專愛，耽於酒色，損德傷年，其言甚切，然終不怨怒也。

translations.literal: In Emperor Cheng's time remonstrating ministers often spoke of the harm of private outings and of female favor with exclusive love, immersion in wine and women, damaging virtue and injuring years—their words very sharp, yet in the end he was never resentful or angry.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Cheng's reign remonstrating ministers often spoke of the harm of private outings, of exclusive female favor, of immersion in wine and women that damaged virtue and shortened life—their words were sharp, yet he was never resentful or angry.

sentences.zh: 寵臣淳于長、張放、史育，育數貶退，家貲不滿千萬，放斥逐就國，長榜死於獄，不以私愛害公義，故雖多內譏，朝廷安平，傳業陛下。

translations.literal: Favored ministers Chunyu Chang, Zhang Fang, and Shi Yu—Yu was repeatedly demoted, family wealth not filling ten million; Fang was expelled and sent to his state; Chang died by beating in prison; he did not let private love harm public righteousness; therefore though there was much inward criticism, the court was secure and calm, and the enterprise passed to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Favored ministers Chunyu Chang, Zhang Fang, and Shi Yu—Yu was repeatedly demoted until his household wealth fell short of ten million; Fang was expelled to his state; Chang died under the rod in prison. He did not let private affection harm public duty; and so though criticism mounted within, the court remained secure and the enterprise passed to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 陛下在國之時，好《詩》、《書》，上儉節，征來，所過道上稱誦德美，此天下所以回心也。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty was in your state, you loved the Odes and Documents, valued thrift and restraint; when summoned, along the roads people praised and recited your virtue—this is why the realm turned its heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty was still in your princely state you loved the Odes and Documents and prized thrift; when you were summoned to the throne, travelers along the roads praised your virtue—this is why the realm turned its heart to you.

sentences.zh: 初即位，易帷帳，去錦繡，乘輿席緣綈繒而已。

translations.literal: At first taking the throne, you changed curtains, removed brocade and embroidery; the imperial carriage's mats were bordered with coarse silk only.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of your reign you changed the curtains, removed brocade and embroidery, and the imperial carriage's mats were bordered with plain silk only.

sentences.zh: 共皇寢廟比當作，憂閔元元，惟用度不足，以義割恩，輒且止息，今始作治。

translations.literal: Lord Gong's resting temple ought by precedent to be built; you grieved for the common people, only because funds were insufficient, cutting affection for righteousness you halted for a time; now construction begins.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Gong's resting temple ought by precedent to be built; you grieved for the common people and, funds being insufficient, cut affection for righteousness and halted work for a time—only now has construction begun.

sentences.zh: 而駙馬都尉董賢亦起官寺上林中，又為賢治大第，開門鄉北闕，引王渠灌園池，使者護作，賞賜吏卒，甚於治宗廟。

translations.literal: Yet Commandant of Cavalry Dong Xian also raised an official temple in Shanglin, and again built a great residence for Xian, opening a gate toward the northern palace gate, drawing the Royal Canal to irrigate garden pools; envoys supervised the work and rewarded clerks and soldiers—more than for building the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Commandant of Cavalry Dong Xian also raised an official temple in Shanglin, and built him a great residence with a gate opening toward the northern palace gate, drawing the Royal Canal to fill his garden pools; envoys supervised the work and rewarded clerks and soldiers—more lavishly than for the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 賢母病，長安廚給祠具，道中過者皆飲食。

translations.literal: When Xian's mother fell ill, the Chang'an kitchen supplied sacrificial implements; passers-by on the road all received food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian's mother fell ill, the Chang'an kitchen supplied sacrificial provisions, and every passer-by on the road was given food and drink.

sentences.zh: 為賢治器，器成，奏御乃行，或物好，特賜其工。

translations.literal: Utensils were made for Xian; when finished they were presented to the emperor before use; if some object was fine, the craftsman was specially rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Utensils were made for Xian; when finished they were presented to the emperor before use, and if some piece was especially fine its craftsman was specially rewarded.

sentences.zh: 自貢獻宗廟、三宮，猶不至此。

translations.literal: Even tribute to the ancestral temple and the Three Palaces did not reach this.
translations.idiomatic: Even tribute to the ancestral temple and the Three Palaces did not go this far.

sentences.zh: 賢家有賓婚及見親，諸官並共，賜及倉頭、奴婢人十萬錢。

translations.literal: When Xian's household had guest weddings or audiences with kin, all offices contributed together; rewards reached even storehouse heads and slave girls—one hundred thousand cash per person.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian's household held guest weddings or kin audiences, all offices contributed together, and rewards reached even storehouse heads and slave girls—one hundred thousand cash per person.

sentences.zh: 使者護視、發取市物，百賈震動，道路讙嘩，群臣惶惑。

translations.literal: Envoys supervised and requisitioned goods from the market; the hundred trades trembled; the roads were noisy with clamor; the ministers were fearful and perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys supervised the markets and requisitioned goods; merchants were shaken; the roads rang with clamor; and the ministers were fearful and perplexed.

sentences.zh: 詔書罷苑，而以賜賢二千餘頃，均田之制從此墮壞。

translations.literal: An edict had abolished the park, yet the land was given to Xian—more than two thousand qing—and the equal-fields system from this collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had abolished the imperial park, yet more than two thousand qing were given to Xian instead, and the equal-fields system collapsed from that moment.

sentences.zh: 奢僭放縱，變亂陰陽，災異眾多，百姓訛言，持籌相驚，天惑其意，不能自止。

translations.literal: Extravagance, presumption, and license disturbed yin and yang; disasters and anomalies were many; the common people spread false reports, holding counting rods and startling one another; Heaven was confused in intent, and he could not stop himself.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagance and presumptuous license disturbed yin and yang; disasters and anomalies multiplied; the people spread false reports and startled one another with counting rods in hand; Heaven's intent was clouded, and he could not stop himself.

sentences.zh: 陛下素仁智慎事，今而有此大譏。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has always been benevolent, wise, and careful in affairs—yet now there is this great reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has always been benevolent, wise, and careful in affairs—yet now draws this great reproach.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『危而不持，顛而不扶，則將安用彼相矣！

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'When it is perilous yet one does not uphold, when it is toppling yet one does not support—then what use is that minister!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'When the state is in peril yet you do not uphold it, when it is toppling yet you do not steady it—what use is that minister!

sentences.zh: 』臣嘉幸得備位，竊內悲傷不能通愚忠之信；

translations.literal: ' Your servant Jia is fortunate to hold a post, yet inwardly grieves in secret, unable to convey the trust of foolish loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: ' Your servant Wang Jia is fortunate to hold office, yet grieves inwardly that he cannot convey the trust of his blunt loyalty;

sentences.zh: 身死有益於國，不敢自惜。

translations.literal: If my body dies yet it benefits the state, I dare not spare myself.
translations.idiomatic: If my death benefits the state, I dare not spare myself.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下慎己之所獨鄉，察眾人之所共疑！

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty be careful where you alone incline, and examine what the multitude jointly doubts!
translations.idiomatic: Only may Your Majesty be careful where you alone incline, and examine what the multitude jointly doubts!

sentences.zh: 往者寵臣鄧通、韓嫣，驕貴失度，逸豫無厭，小人不勝情慾，卒陷罪辜，亂國亡軀，不終其祿，所謂『愛之適足以害之』者也！

translations.literal: Formerly favored ministers Deng Tong and Han Yan—arrogant in honor beyond measure, dissolute pleasure without satiety—petty men unable to master emotion and desire, in the end fell into crime and guilt, disordering the state and losing their bodies, not finishing their stipends: what is called 'to love them is just enough to harm them'!
translations.idiomatic: Formerly favored ministers Deng Tong and Han Yan grew arrogant beyond measure in their honors, dissolute and insatiable—petty men who could not master desire, they fell at last into crime, disordering the state and losing their lives without finishing their stipends: what men call 'love them just enough to destroy them'!

sentences.zh: 宜深覽前世，以節賢寵，全安其命。

translations.literal: You ought deeply to review former ages, thereby to restrain Xian's favor and wholly preserve his life.
translations.idiomatic: You ought deeply to review former ages, restrain favor toward Xian, and preserve his life entire.

sentences.zh: 」上由是於嘉浸不說。

translations.literal: " From this the emperor grew gradually displeased with Jia.
translations.idiomatic: " From this the emperor grew gradually displeased with Wang Jia.

sentences.zh: 前涼州刺史杜鄴以方正對策曰：「臣聞陽尊陰卑，天之道也。

translations.literal: Former Governor of Liangzhou Du Ye, answering as worthy and upright, said: "Your servant has heard that yang is honored and yin is lowly—this is Heaven's Way.
translations.idiomatic: Former Governor of Liangzhou Du Ye, answering as worthy and upright, said: "Your servant has heard that yang is honored and yin is lowly—this is Heaven's Way.

sentences.zh: 是以男雖賤，各為其家陽，女雖貴，猶為其國陰。

translations.literal: Therefore though a man may be lowly, each is the yang of his household; though a woman may be honored, she is still the yin of her state.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore though a man may be lowly, each is the yang of his household; though a woman may be honored, she remains the yin of her state.

sentences.zh: 故禮明三從之義，雖有文母之德，必繫於子。

translations.literal: Hence ritual clarifies the meaning of the Three Followings: though one has the virtue of a civil mother, she must be tied to her son.
translations.idiomatic: Hence ritual clarifies the Three Followings: though a woman has the virtue of a civil mother, she must be bound to her son.

sentences.zh: 昔鄭伯隨姜氏之欲，終有叔段篡國之禍；

translations.literal: Formerly the Earl of Zheng followed Lady Jiang's desires, and in the end had the disaster of Uncle Duan usurping the state;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Earl of Zheng followed Lady Jiang's desires, and in the end suffered Uncle Duan's usurpation;

sentences.zh: 周襄王內迫惠後之難，而遭居鄭之危。

translations.literal: King Xiang of Zhou, inwardly pressed by Queen Hui's difficulty, met the peril of dwelling in Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: King Xiang of Zhou, pressed from within by Queen Hui, met the peril of taking refuge in Zheng.

sentences.zh: 漢興，呂太后權私親屬，幾危社稷。

translations.literal: When Han arose, Empress Dowager Lü used power for private kin and nearly endangered the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Han arose, Empress Dowager Lü wielded power for her private kin and nearly endangered the realm.

sentences.zh: 竊見陛下約儉正身，欲與天下更始，然嘉瑞未應，而日食、地震。

translations.literal: Your servant has seen that Your Majesty is abstemious and corrects the person, wishing with the realm to make a new beginning—yet fine omens have not responded, while there is solar eclipse and earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant sees that Your Majesty is abstemious and upright in person, wishing to make a new beginning with the realm—yet fine omens have not answered, while there are solar eclipse and earthquake.

sentences.zh: 案《春秋》災異，以指象為言語。

translations.literal: Examining the Spring and Autumn Annals' disasters and anomalies, they take pointing images as speech.
translations.idiomatic: Examining disasters and anomalies in the Spring and Autumn Annals, they speak through pointing images.

sentences.zh: 日食，明陽為陰所臨。

translations.literal: Solar eclipse: bright yang is overspread by yin.
translations.idiomatic: A solar eclipse means bright yang is overspread by yin.

sentences.zh: 坤以法地，為土，為母，以安靜為德；

translations.literal: Kun takes earth as its model, is soil, is mother, and takes quiet calm as virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Kun models itself on earth—it is soil, it is mother, and its virtue is quiet calm;

sentences.zh: 震，不陰之效也。

translations.literal: quake is the effect of yin not being yin.
translations.idiomatic: earthquake is the effect of yin failing to remain yin.

sentences.zh: 占像甚明，臣敢不直言其事！

translations.literal: The omen-image is very clear; your servant dares not fail to speak plainly of the matter!
translations.idiomatic: The omen-image is very clear; your servant dares not fail to speak plainly!

sentences.zh: 昔曾子問從令之義，孔子曰：『是何言與！

translations.literal: Formerly Zengzi asked the meaning of following orders; Confucius said: 'What words are these!
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Zengzi asked the meaning of following a parent's orders; Confucius said, 'What words are these!

sentences.zh: 』善閔子騫守禮不苟從親，所行無非理者，故無可間也。

translations.literal: ' The good Min Ziqian kept ritual and would not casually follow kin; what he did was never against reason—hence there was nothing to pick at.
translations.idiomatic: ' The good Min Ziqian kept ritual and would not casually obey kin; nothing he did was against reason—hence there was nothing to criticize.

sentences.zh: 今諸外家昆弟，無賢不肖，並侍帷幄，布在列位，或典兵衛，或將軍屯，寵意並於一家，積貴之勢，世所希見、所希聞也。

translations.literal: Now the various affinal kin and brothers, worthy or not, all attend the curtains, spread through the ranks; some command military guard, some lead encamped armies; favor and intent concentrate on one house—the accumulated weight of honor is what the age rarely sees or hears.
translations.idiomatic: Now the various affinal kin and brothers, worthy or not, all attend the curtains and fill the ranks; some command military guard, some lead encamped armies—favor concentrates on one house in a weight of honor the age has rarely seen or heard.

sentences.zh: 至乃並置大司馬、將軍之官，皇甫雖盛，三桓雖隆，魯為作三軍，無以甚此！

translations.literal: They even set up together the offices of Grand Marshal and general; though Huangfu was strong, though the Three Huan were exalted, though Lu made three armies—nothing surpasses this!
translations.idiomatic: They even set up together the offices of Grand Marshal and general; though Huangfu was strong, though the Three Huan were exalted, though Lu raised three armies—nothing surpasses this!

sentences.zh: 當拜之日，晻然日食。

translations.literal: On the day of appointment, dim eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of their appointment the sun was dimly eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 不在前後，臨事而發者，明陛下謙遜無專，承指非一，所言輒聽，所欲輒隨，有罪惡者不坐辜罰，無功能者畢受官爵，流漸積畏，過在於是，欲令昭昭以覺聖朝。

translations.literal: Not before or after but as the affair unfolded—this shows Your Majesty's modesty without sole authority, receiving pointers not from one alone: what is spoken is at once heard, what is desired is at once followed; those with guilt and evil are not seated in punishment, those without merit or ability all receive rank and fief; the stream gradually accumulates dread—the fault lies here; I wish to make it bright and clear to awaken the sage court.
translations.idiomatic: Not before or after but as the affair unfolded—this shows Your Majesty's modesty without sole authority, receiving direction from more than one voice: what is spoken is at once heard, what is desired is at once granted; the guilty go unpunished, the meritless all receive rank and fief; dread accumulates by degrees—the fault lies here, and I wish to make it plain to awaken the sage court.

sentences.zh: 昔詩人所刺，《春秋》所譏，指象如此，殆不在它。

translations.literal: What poets of old satirized, what the Spring and Autumn Annals reproached—pointing images like this; probably not in anything else.
translations.idiomatic: What poets of old satirized and the Spring and Autumn Annals reproached points to images like these—probably to nothing else.

sentences.zh: 由後視前，忿邑非之。

translations.literal: Viewing the former from the latter, one is angry and deplores it.
translations.idiomatic: Viewing the past from the future, men grow angry and deplore such things.

sentences.zh: 逮身所行，不自鏡見，則以為可，計之過者。

translations.literal: When it reaches what one's own person does, if one does not mirror and see oneself, one thinks it acceptable—this is excess in reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: But when it comes to what one's own person does, if one does not mirror oneself, one thinks it acceptable—this is excess in judgment.

sentences.zh: 願陛下加致精誠，思承始初，事稽諸古，以厭下心，則黎庶群生無不說喜，上帝百神收還威怒，禎祥福祿，何嫌不報！

translations.literal: May Your Majesty increase and extend refined sincerity, think to continue the beginning, affairs examined against antiquity, thereby to satisfy the heart below—then the black-headed masses and all living things will none fail to rejoice; the High Lord and the hundred spirits will gather back wrath and anger; auspicious omens, fortune, and stipend—what worry that they will not respond!
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty increase refined sincerity, think to continue your beginning, and weigh affairs against antiquity to satisfy the hearts below—then the people will all rejoice, the High Lord and the hundred spirits will withdraw their wrath, and auspicious omens, fortune, and blessings—what worry that they will not answer!

sentences.zh: 上又征孔光詣公車，問以日食事，拜為光祿大夫，秩中二千石，給事中，位次丞相。

translations.literal: The emperor also summoned Kong Guang to the imperial carriage office, questioned him on the eclipse affair, and appointed him Grand Master of Splendor at rank 2000-shi, Palace Attendant Within the Gates, rank next after the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also summoned Kong Guang to the imperial carriage office, questioned him about the eclipse, and appointed him Grand Master of Splendor at rank 2000-shi, as Palace Attendant Within the Gates with rank next after the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 初，王莽既就國，杜門自守。

translations.literal: Initially, after Wang Mang had gone to his state, he shut his doors and kept himself guarded.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Wang Mang had gone to his state, he shut his doors and kept to himself.

sentences.zh: 其中子獲殺奴，莽切責獲，令自殺。

translations.literal: His middle son Huo killed a slave; Mang sternly reproached Huo and ordered him to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: His middle son Wang Huo killed a slave; Wang Mang sternly reproached him and ordered him to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 在國三歲，吏民上書冤訟莽者百數。

translations.literal: Three years in his state, officials and people submitted memorials pleading Mang's injustice—several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: During three years in his state, officials and commoners submitted several hundred memorials pleading Wang Mang's injustice.

sentences.zh: 至是，賢良周護、宋崇等對策，復深訟莽功德。

translations.literal: At this time the worthies Zhou Hu and Song Chong and others, answering in audience, again deeply pleaded Mang's merit and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the worthies Zhou Hu and Song Chong and others, answering in audience, again deeply praised Wang Mang's merit and virtue.

sentences.zh: 上於是征莽及平阿侯仁還京師，侍太后。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon summoned Mang and Marquis of Ping'e Ren back to the capital to attend the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon summoned Wang Mang and Marquis of Ping'e Liu Ren back to the capital to attend the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 董賢因日食之變以沮傅晏、息夫躬之策，辛卯，上收晏印綬，罷就第。

translations.literal: Dong Xian used the eclipse omen to thwart Fu Yan and Xinfu Gong's plans; on xinmao the emperor took back Yan's seal and ribbon and dismissed him to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xian used the eclipse omen to thwart Fu Yan and Xinfu Gong's plans; on xinmao the emperor took back Fu Yan's seal and ribbon and sent him to his residence.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，皇太太后傅氏崩，合葬渭陵，稱孝元傅皇后。

translations.literal: On dingsi the Grand Imperial Empress Dowager Fu died; she was buried jointly at Weiling and styled Empress Fu, filial to Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the Grand Imperial Empress Dowager Fu died; she was buried jointly at Weiling and styled Empress Fu, filial consort of Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 丞相、御史奏息夫躬、孫寵等罪過，上乃免躬、寵官，遣就國；

translations.literal: The Chancellor and Censor memorialized Xinfu Gong, Sun Chong, and others' crimes and faults; the emperor then removed Gong and Chong from office and sent them to their states;
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor and Censor memorialized the crimes of Xinfu Gong, Sun Chong, and others; the emperor removed Gong and Chong from office and sent them to their states;

sentences.zh: 又罷侍中、諸曹、黃門郎數十人。

translations.literal: He also dismissed several tens of Palace Attendants, various bureau officers, and Yellow Gate Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He also dismissed several dozen Palace Attendants, bureau officers, and Yellow Gate Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 鮑宣上書曰：「陛下父事天，母事地，子養黎民。

translations.literal: Bao Xuan submitted a memorial, saying: "Your Majesty serves Heaven as father, Earth as mother, and nourishes the black-headed people as children.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xuan submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty serves Heaven as father, Earth as mother, and nourishes the people as children.

sentences.zh: 即位已來，父虧明，母震動，子訛言相驚恐。

translations.literal: Since taking the throne, the father has lost brightness, the mother has quaked, the children spread false reports and startle one another in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking the throne, the father has lost his brightness, the mother has quaked, and the children spread false reports in mutual terror.

sentences.zh: 今日食於三始，誠可畏懼。

translations.literal: Today the eclipse at the Three Beginnings is truly fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Today's eclipse at the Three Beginnings is truly fearful.

sentences.zh: 小民正朔日尚恐毀敗器物，何況於日虧乎！

translations.literal: Petty folk on the new-year day still fear damaging and breaking utensils—how much more when the sun is diminished!
translations.idiomatic: Common folk on New Year's Day still fear damaging their utensils—how much more when the sun itself is diminished!

sentences.zh: 陛下深內自責，避正殿，舉直言，求過失，罷退外親及旁仄素餐之人，征拜孔光為光祿大夫，發覺孫寵、息夫躬過惡，免官遣就國，眾庶歙然，莫不說喜。

translations.literal: Your Majesty deeply blamed yourself within, avoided the main hall, raised frank speech, sought faults, dismissed affinal kin and lateral parasites who eat salary without work, summoned and appointed Kong Guang Grand Master of Splendor, exposed Sun Chong and Xinfu Gong's excesses and evils, removed them from office and sent them to their states—the multitude sighed with relief; none failed to rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty blamed yourself deeply within, avoided the main hall, raised frank speech, sought faults, dismissed affinal kin and lateral parasites who drew salary without work, summoned Kong Guang as Grand Master of Splendor, exposed Sun Chong and Xinfu Gong's excesses, removed them and sent them to their states—and the multitude sighed with relief; none failed to rejoice.

sentences.zh: 天人同心，人心說則天意解矣。

translations.literal: Heaven and men share one heart; when men's hearts are pleased, Heaven's intent is released.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and men share one heart; when the people's hearts are pleased, Heaven's intent is released.

sentences.zh: 乃二月丙戌，白虹干日，連陰不雨，此天下憂結未解，民有怨望未塞者也。

translations.literal: Yet on the second month bingxu, a white rainbow crossed the sun, overcast without rain for days—this is the realm's worry-knot not yet loosened, the people's resentful gaze not yet filled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet on the second month bingxu a white rainbow crossed the sun and clouds lingered without rain—this shows the realm's worry not yet loosened and the people's resentful gaze not yet satisfied.

sentences.zh: 侍中、駙馬都尉董賢，本無葭莩之親，但以令色、諛言自進，賞賜無度，竭盡府臧，併合三第，尚以為小，復壞暴室。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant and Commandant of Cavalry Dong Xian originally had no reed-and-fluff kinship, yet by pleasing looks and flattery advanced himself; rewards without measure exhausted the treasury stores; he merged three great residences and still thought them small, and again destroyed the Bao chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant and Commandant of Cavalry Dong Xian had no reed-and-fluff kinship with you, yet advanced himself by pleasing looks and flattery; his rewards knew no limit and exhausted the treasury; he merged three great residences and still thought them small, and again destroyed the Bao chamber.

sentences.zh: 賢父、子坐使天子使者，將作治第，行夜吏卒皆得賞賜，上塚有會，輒太官為供。

translations.literal: Xian's father and son sat while making the Son of Heaven's envoys and the Chief of Construction build residences; night patrol clerks and soldiers all received rewards; whenever there was a gathering at the ancestral mound, the Grand Provisioner supplied the feast.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's father and son sat at ease while the Son of Heaven's envoys and the Chief of Construction built their residences; night patrol clerks and soldiers all received rewards; whenever there was a gathering at the ancestral mound, the Grand Provisioner supplied the feast.

sentences.zh: 海內貢獻，當養一君，今反盡之賢家，豈天意與民意邪！

translations.literal: Tribute from within the seas ought to nourish one lord—now instead it is all poured into Xian's house; can this be Heaven's intent and the people's will!
translations.idiomatic: Tribute from within the seas ought to nourish one ruler—now it is all poured into Xian's house; can this be Heaven's intent or the people's will!

sentences.zh: 天不可久負，厚之如此，反所以害之也！

translations.literal: Heaven cannot long be burdened; to thicken him thus is instead how to harm him!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven cannot long be burdened; to heap favor on him thus is instead how to destroy him!

sentences.zh: 誠欲哀賢，宜為謝過天地，解讎海內，免遣就國，收乘輿器物還之縣官，如此，可以父子終其性命；

translations.literal: If you truly wish to pity Xian, you ought apologize to Heaven and Earth for faults, dissolve enmity within the seas, remove him and send him to his state, take back imperial-carriage utensils and return them to the government offices—thus father and son may finish their lives;
translations.idiomatic: If you truly wish to pity Xian, you ought apologize to Heaven and Earth, dissolve enmity within the seas, remove him and send him to his state, take back imperial-carriage utensils and return them to the government—thus father and son may live out their lives;

sentences.zh: 不者，海內之所仇，未有得久安者也。

translations.literal: If not, he will be what the realm hates, and none have long obtained peace.
translations.idiomatic: If not, he will be what the realm hates, and none in such a case have long remained secure.

sentences.zh: 孫寵、息夫躬不宜居國，可皆免，以視天下。

translations.literal: Sun Chong and Xinfu Gong ought not dwell in their states; all may be removed, to show the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chong and Xinfu Gong ought not remain in their states; remove them all, to show the realm.

sentences.zh: 復征何武、師丹、彭宣、傅喜，曠然使民易視，以應天心，建立大政，興太平之端。

translations.literal: Again summon He Wu, Shi Dan, Peng Xuan, and Fu Xi; open the view so the people change what they see, to answer Heaven's heart, establish great government, and raise the beginning of great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Again summon He Wu, Shi Dan, Peng Xuan, and Fu Xi; open the view so the people change what they see, answer Heaven's heart, establish great government, and raise the beginning of great peace.

sentences.zh: 」上感大異，納宣言，征何武、彭宣；

translations.literal: " The emperor was moved by the great anomalies, adopted Xuan's words, and summoned He Wu and Peng Xuan;
translations.idiomatic: " Moved by the great anomalies, the emperor adopted Bao Xuan's words and summoned He Wu and Peng Xuan;

sentences.zh: 拜鮑宣為司隸。

translations.literal: He appointed Bao Xuan Metropolitan Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Bao Xuan Metropolitan Commandant.

sentences.zh: 上托傅太后遺詔，令太皇太后下丞相、御史，益封董賢二千戶，賜孔鄉侯、汝昌侯、陽新侯國。

translations.literal: The emperor used Empress Dowager Fu's testamentary edict to have the Grand Empress Dowager issue to the Chancellor and Censor an increase of Dong Xian's fief by two thousand households, and grant states to Marquis of Kongxiang, Marquis of Ruchang, and Marquis of Yangxin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor used Empress Dowager Fu's testamentary edict to have the Grand Empress Dowager instruct the Chancellor and Censor to increase Dong Xian's fief by two thousand households and grant states to Marquis of Kongxiang, Marquis of Ruchang, and Marquis of Yangxin.

sentences.zh: 王嘉封還詔書，因奏封事諫曰：「臣聞爵祿、土地，天之有也。

translations.literal: Wang Jia sealed and returned the edict document, and submitted a sealed memorial remonstrating, saying: "Your servant has heard that ranks, stipends, and land belong to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia sealed and returned the edict, and submitted a sealed remonstrance: "Your servant has heard that ranks, stipends, and land belong to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 《書》云：『天命有德，五服五章哉！

translations.literal: The Documents say: 'Heaven's mandate is to the virtuous—five garments and five patterns!
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say, 'Heaven's mandate rests on the virtuous—five garments and five patterns!

sentences.zh: 』王者代天爵人，尤宜慎之。

translations.literal: ' The king replaces Heaven in enfeoffing men—he ought especially to be careful.
translations.idiomatic: ' The king enfeoffs men on Heaven's behalf—he ought especially to be careful.

sentences.zh: 裂地而封，不得其宜，則眾庶不服，感動陰陽，其害疾自深。

translations.literal: Splitting land to enfeoff, if not fitting in place, then the multitude will not submit; yin and yang are stirred—the harm quickly deepens of itself.
translations.idiomatic: To split land and enfeoff where it is not fitting is to make the multitude refuse submission and stir yin and yang—the harm quickly deepens of itself.

sentences.zh: 今聖體久不平，此臣嘉所內懼也。

translations.literal: Now the sage person long unwell—this is what your servant Jia inwardly fears.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty's person has long been unwell—this is what your servant Wang Jia inwardly fears.

sentences.zh: 高安侯賢，佞幸之臣，陛下傾爵位以貴之，單貨財以富之，損至尊以寵之，主威已黜，府臧已竭，唯恐不足。

translations.literal: Marquis of Gao'an Xian is a fawning favorite; Your Majesty tilts rank and office to honor him, pours goods and wealth to enrich him, diminishes the august ultimate to favor him—sovereign authority is already dimmed, treasury stores already drained, yet still fearing it is not enough.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Gao'an Dong Xian is a fawning favorite; Your Majesty tilts rank and office to honor him, pours out goods and wealth to enrich him, diminishes your own majesty to favor him—sovereign authority is already dimmed, the treasury already drained, yet you still fear it is not enough.

sentences.zh: 財皆民力所為，孝文皇帝欲起露台，重百金之費，克己不作。

translations.literal: Wealth is all what the people's strength produced; Emperor Wen wished to raise a terrace in the open air, weighed the cost of a hundred gold, restrained himself and did not build.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth is all produced by the people's strength; Emperor Wen wished to raise an open-air terrace, weighed the cost at a hundred gold, restrained himself, and did not build.

sentences.zh: 今賢散公賦以施私惠，一家至受千金，往古以來，貴臣未嘗有此，流聞四方，皆同怨之。

translations.literal: Now Xian disperses public levies to bestow private favor; one household has received up to a thousand gold; from antiquity until now honored ministers have never had this; it flows and is heard in the four quarters—all alike resent it.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xian disperses public levies to bestow private favor; one household has received as much as a thousand gold; from antiquity until now no honored minister has had this; word spreads to the four quarters and all alike resent it.

sentences.zh: 里諺曰：『千人所指，無病而死，』臣常為之寒心。

translations.literal: A village saying runs: 'A thousand men point at you—without illness you die'; your servant is often chilled in heart for it.
translations.idiomatic: A village saying runs, 'When a thousand men point at you, you die without illness'—your servant is often chilled at heart for it.

sentences.zh: 今太皇太后以永信太后遺詔詔丞相、御史，益賢戶，賜三侯國，臣嘉竊惑。

translations.literal: Now the Grand Empress Dowager, by Everlasting Faith Empress Dowager's testamentary edict, has edicted the Chancellor and Censor to increase Xian's households and grant three marquis states—your servant Jia is privately perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Grand Empress Dowager, by Everlasting Faith Empress Dowager's testamentary edict, has instructed the Chancellor and Censor to increase Xian's households and grant three marquis states—your servant Wang Jia is privately perplexed.

sentences.zh: 山崩、地動、日食於三朝，皆陰侵陽之戒也。

translations.literal: Mountain collapse, earth quake, eclipse at the Three Beginnings—all are warnings of yin invading yang.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain collapse, earthquake, and eclipse at the Three Beginnings are all warnings of yin invading yang.

sentences.zh: 前賢已再封，晏、商再易邑，業緣私橫求，恩已過厚，求索自恣，不知厭足，甚傷尊尊之義，不可以示天下，為害痛矣！

translations.literal: The former worthy has already been enfeoffed twice; Yan and Shang have twice changed their fiefs; Ye by private ties sought wildly—grace already past thick, seeking and asking at will, not knowing satiety—greatly injuring the meaning of honoring the honored; this cannot be shown to the realm; the harm is grievous!
translations.idiomatic: The former favorite has already been enfeoffed twice; Fu Yan and Fu Shang have twice changed their fiefs; Fu Ye sought wildly through private ties—favor already past thick, demanding at will without satiety—greatly injuring the meaning of honoring the honored; this cannot be shown to the realm; the harm is grievous!

sentences.zh: 臣驕侵罔，陰陽失節，氣感相動，害及身體。

translations.literal: Ministers arrogant and encroaching deceive; yin and yang lose their measure; qi-stimulus moves mutually—the harm reaches the body.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers grow arrogant and encroaching, yin and yang lose their measure; responsive forces move one another and harm reaches the body.

sentences.zh: 陛下寢疾久不平，繼嗣未立，宜思正萬事，順天人之心，以求福祐，奈何輕身肆意，不念高祖之勤苦，垂立制度，欲傳之於無窮哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty's long illness unabated, succession not yet established—you ought think to rectify the ten thousand affairs, follow Heaven and men's hearts to seek blessing and protection; why lightly abandon the person and indulge the will, not recalling Gaozu's toil, the system he left hanging down, wishing to pass it to without end!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's illness has long been unabated and the succession is not yet established—you ought think to rectify the ten thousand affairs and follow Heaven and the people's hearts to seek blessing; why lightly indulge your will, not recalling Gaozu's toil and the system he left hanging down, wishing to pass it on without end!

sentences.zh: 臣謹封上詔書，不敢露見。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully seals and submits the edict document, not daring to expose it for view.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant respectfully seals and submits the edict, not daring to expose it for view.

sentences.zh: 非愛死而不自法，恐天下聞之，故不敢自劾。

translations.literal: It is not that I cherish death yet will not apply the law to myself—I fear the realm will hear of it; therefore I dare not impeach myself.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that I welcome death yet refuse to punish myself—I fear the realm will hear of it; therefore I dare not impeach myself.

sentences.zh: 初，廷尉梁相治東平王雲獄，時冬月未盡二旬，而相心疑雲冤獄，有飾辭，奏欲傳之長安，更下公卿覆治。

translations.literal: Initially, Minister of Justice Liang Xiang handled the prison case of King Yun of Dongping; it was winter and not yet twenty days into the month, yet Xiang inwardly suspected Yun's case was a wrongful conviction with embellished statements; he memorialized wishing to transfer it to Chang'an for the high ministers to re-examine.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Minister of Justice Liang Xiang handled the case of King Yun of Dongping; winter had not yet run twenty days, yet Xiang suspected a wrongful conviction with embellished testimony and memorialized to transfer the case to Chang'an for re-examination by the high ministers.

sentences.zh: 尚書令鞫譚、僕射宗伯鳳以為可許。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Ju Tan and Vice Director Zong Bo Feng thought it could be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Ju Tan and Vice Director Zong Bo Feng thought the request could be granted.

sentences.zh: 天子以為相等皆見上體不平，外內顧望，操持兩心，幸雲逾冬，無討賊疾惡主讎之意，免相等皆為庶人。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven thought Liang Xiang and the others all saw the sovereign's health was poor, looked inward and outward with hesitation, held two minds, hoped Yun would pass winter, and had no mind to pursue villains and hate evil for the sovereign's sake—he dismissed Liang Xiang and all as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor concluded that Liang Xiang and the others had seen his health fail, wavered inwardly and outwardly, held two minds, and hoped Yun would survive the winter—showing no zeal to pursue villains and avenge their lord; he dismissed Liang Xiang and all the rest to commoner rank.

sentences.zh: 後數月，大赦，嘉薦「相等皆有材行，聖王有計功除過，臣竊為朝廷惜此三人。

translations.literal: Several months later, at a general amnesty, Jia recommended: "Liang Xiang and the others all have talent and conduct; sage kings reckon merit and remove faults; your servant privately grieves for the court to lose these three men."
translations.idiomatic: Several months later, at a general amnesty, Wang Jia recommended: "Liang Xiang and the others all have talent and character; sage kings weigh merit and pardon faults; your servant privately grieves for the court to lose these three men."

sentences.zh: 」書奏，上不能平。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted; the emperor could not be at peace with it.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was submitted; the emperor could not accept it calmly.

sentences.zh: 後二十餘日，嘉封還益董賢戶事，上乃發怒，召嘉詣尚書，責問以「相等前坐不忠，罪惡著聞，君時輒已自劾；

translations.literal: More than twenty days later, when Jia's enfeoffment was returned to increase Dong Xian's household affairs, the emperor then flew into rage, summoned Jia to the Secretariat, and reproached him: "Liang Xiang and the others previously sat for disloyalty; their crimes are publicly known; you then promptly self-impeached;
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty days later, when Wang Jia's fief was returned to augment Dong Xian's household, the emperor flew into a rage, summoned Jia to the Secretariat, and reproached him: "Liang Xiang and the others were earlier convicted of disloyalty; their crimes are publicly known; you then promptly impeached yourself;

sentences.zh: 今又稱譽，云『為朝廷惜之』，何也？

translations.literal: now again you praise them, saying 'grieve for the court to lose them'—how is this?
translations.idiomatic: now again you praise them, saying you grieve for the court to lose them—how is this?"

sentences.zh: 」嘉免冠謝罪。

translations.literal: " Jia removed his cap and apologized for guilt.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jia removed his cap and apologized.

sentences.zh: 事下將軍中朝者，光祿大夫孔光等劾「嘉迷國罔上，不道，請謁者召嘉詣廷尉詔獄。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to generals and inner-court officials; Palace Chamberlain Kong Guang and others impeached: "Jia deluded the state and deceived the sovereign, unfilial—we request the usher summon Jia to the Minister of Justice imperial prison."
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to generals and inner-court officials; Palace Chamberlain Kong Guang and others impeached: "Jia deluded the state and deceived the sovereign—unfilial; we request an usher summon Jia to the imperial prison under the Minister of Justice."

sentences.zh: 」議郎龔等以為「嘉言事前後相違，宜奪爵土，免為庶人。

translations.literal: " Remonstrance Gentleman Gong and others held: "Jia's words before and after contradict each other—it is fitting to strip rank and fief and dismiss him as a commoner."
translations.idiomatic: " Remonstrance Gentleman Gong and others held: "Jia's statements before and after contradict each other—strip his rank and fief and reduce him to commoner status."

sentences.zh: 」永信少府猛等以為「嘉罪名雖應法，大臣括發關械，裸躬就笞，非所以重國，褒宗廟也。

translations.literal: " Director of the Ever-Faithful Palace Meng and others held: "Though Jia's crimes answer to the law, to bind a great minister's hair, put him in shackles, bare his body, and submit to beating is not the means to honor the state and exalt the ancestral temple."
translations.idiomatic: " Director of the Ever-Faithful Palace Meng and others held: "Though Jia's crimes answer to the law, to bind a great minister's hair, shackle him, bare his body, and beat him is not how to honor the state and exalt the ancestral temple."

sentences.zh: 」上不聽，三月，詔「假謁者節，召丞相詣廷尉詔獄。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not listen; in the third month an edict said: "Lend the usher's staff; summon the chancellor to the Minister of Justice imperial prison."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not hear it; in the third month an edict said: "Lend the usher's staff; summon the chancellor to the imperial prison under the Minister of Justice."

sentences.zh: 使者既到，府掾、史涕泣，共和藥進嘉，嘉不肯服。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived, the chancellor's clerks and scribes wept and together offered medicine to Jia; Jia refused to take it.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy arrived, the chancellor's clerks and scribes wept and together offered poison to Jia; Jia refused to take it.

sentences.zh: 主簿曰：「將相不對理陳冤，相踵以為故事，君侯宜引決。

translations.literal: The chief clerk said: "Generals and chancellors do not plead their case at trial to state their grievance—one after another they took this as precedent; my lord ought to resolve matters by his own hand."
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk said: "Generals and chancellors do not plead their case at trial—one after another they made this the precedent; my lord ought to take his own life."

sentences.zh: 」使者危坐府門上，主簿復前進藥。

translations.literal: " The envoy sat upright at the mansion gate; the chief clerk again advanced the medicine.
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy sat upright at the mansion gate; the chief clerk again advanced the poison.

sentences.zh: 嘉引藥杯以擊地，謂官屬曰：「丞相幸得備位三公，奉職負國，當伏刑都市，以示萬眾。

translations.literal: Jia raised the medicine cup and struck the ground with it, saying to his officials: "The chancellor, having fortunately attained one of the Three Ducal posts, bears office and owes the state—he ought to submit to execution in the marketplace to show the myriad masses."
translations.idiomatic: Jia raised the cup and dashed it to the ground, telling his staff: "A chancellor who has attained one of the Three Ducal posts bears office and owes the state—he ought to die by public execution in the marketplace, as an example to all."

sentences.zh: 丞相豈兒女子邪！

translations.literal: Is the chancellor a mere child or woman!
translations.idiomatic: Is a chancellor a child or a woman!

sentences.zh: 何謂咀藥而死！

translations.literal: Why speak of chewing medicine to die!
translations.idiomatic: Why speak of swallowing poison to die!

sentences.zh: 」嘉遂裝，出見使者，再拜受詔；

translations.literal: " Jia thereupon dressed, went out to see the envoy, twice bowed and received the edict;
translations.idiomatic: " Jia thereupon dressed, went out to see the envoy, bowed twice and received the edict;

sentences.zh: 乘吏小車，去蓋，不冠，隨使者詣廷尉。

translations.literal: he rode a clerk's small cart, removed the canopy, went bareheaded, and followed the envoy to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: he rode a clerk's small cart, removed the canopy, went bareheaded, and followed the envoy to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 廷尉收嘉丞相、新甫侯印綬，縛嘉載致都船詔獄。

translations.literal: The Minister of Justice took Jia's chancellor and Marquis of Xinfu seals and cords, bound Jia, and conveyed him to the Metropolitan Boat imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Justice took Jia's chancellor and Marquis of Xinfu seals and cords, bound him, and conveyed him to the Metropolitan Boat imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 上聞嘉生自詣吏，大怒，使將軍以下與五二千石雜治。

translations.literal: The emperor heard Jia had gone alive of his own accord to the officials and was greatly angered; he ordered generals downward and the five-hundred- and two-thousand-picul ranks to conduct a joint trial.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Jia had gone alive of his own accord to the officials, the emperor was furious and ordered generals and the five-hundred- and two-thousand-picul ranks to conduct a joint trial.

sentences.zh: 吏詰問嘉，嘉對曰：「案事者思得實。

translations.literal: The officials interrogated Jia; Jia replied: "Those who handle cases think to obtain the truth.
translations.idiomatic: The officials interrogated Jia; Jia replied: "Those who handle cases seek the truth.

sentences.zh: 竊見相等前治東平王獄，不以雲為不當死，欲關公卿，示重慎，誠不見其外內顧望，阿附為雲驗，復幸得蒙大赦。

translations.literal: Your servant has seen that when Liang Xiang and the others earlier handled King Yun of Dongping's prison case, they did not hold that Yun ought not to die; they wished to refer it to the high ministers to show weighty caution—truly I did not see them looking inward and outward with hesitation, currying favor to manufacture evidence for Yun; they again fortunately received the great amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant observed that when Liang Xiang and the others handled King Yun's case, they did not hold that Yun ought not to die; they wished to refer it to the high ministers to show weighty caution—I truly did not see them wavering inwardly and outwardly or currying favor to manufacture evidence for Yun; they again fortunately received the great amnesty."

sentences.zh: 相等皆良善吏，臣竊為國惜賢，不私此三人。

translations.literal: Liang Xiang and the others are all good and worthy officials; your servant privately grieves for the state to lose the worthy—not out of private favor for these three men."
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xiang and the others are all capable officials; your servant grieves for the state to lose worthy men—not out of private favor for these three."

sentences.zh: 」獄吏曰：「苟如此，則君何以為罪？

translations.literal: " The prison clerk said: "If it is so, then on what ground is my lord guilty?
translations.idiomatic: " The prison clerk said: "If that is so, then on what ground is my lord guilty?

sentences.zh: 猶當有以負國，不空入獄矣。

translations.literal: There must still be some way you have failed the state—you cannot enter prison for nothing."
translations.idiomatic: There must still be some way you have failed the state—you cannot enter prison for nothing."

sentences.zh: 」吏稍侵辱嘉，嘉喟然仰天歎曰：「幸得充備宰相，不能進賢、退不肖，以是負國，死有餘責。

translations.literal: " The officials gradually insulted Jia; Jia sighed, looked up to Heaven, and said: "Having fortunately filled the chancellor's post, I could not advance the worthy and remove the unworthy—thereby failing the state; death still leaves guilt remaining."
translations.idiomatic: " The officials gradually insulted him; Jia sighed, looked up to Heaven, and said: "Having attained the chancellorship, I could not advance the worthy and remove the unworthy—thereby failing the state; death still leaves guilt remaining."

sentences.zh: 」吏問賢、不肖主名。

translations.literal: " The officials asked the names of the worthy and unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: " The officials asked the names of the worthy and unworthy.

sentences.zh: 嘉曰：「賢：故丞相孔光、故大司空何武，不能進；

translations.literal: Jia said: "Worthy: former Chancellor Kong Guang and former Grand Minister of Works He Wu—I could not advance them;
translations.idiomatic: Jia said: "Worthy: former Chancellor Kong Guang and former Grand Minister of Works He Wu—I could not advance them;

sentences.zh: 惡：高安侯董賢父子，佞邪亂朝，而不能退。

translations.literal: wicked: Marquis of Gao'an Dong Xian, father and son—fawning and wicked, throwing the court into disorder—and I could not remove them.
translations.idiomatic: wicked: Marquis of Gao'an Dong Xian, father and son—fawning and wicked, throwing the court into disorder—and I could not remove them.

sentences.zh: 罪當死，死無所恨！

translations.literal: The crime deserves death; in death I have no regret!
translations.idiomatic: The crime deserves death; in death I have no regret!

sentences.zh: 」嘉繫獄二十餘日，不食，歐血而死。

translations.literal: " Jia was bound in prison more than twenty days, ate nothing, vomited blood, and died.
translations.idiomatic: " Jia was bound in prison more than twenty days, ate nothing, vomited blood, and died.

sentences.zh: 已而上覽其對，思嘉言，會御史大夫賈延免，夏，五月，乙卯，以孔光為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor reviewed his replies, reflected on Jia's words; it happened Censor-in-Chief Jia Yan was dismissed—in summer, the fifth month, on yimao, Kong Guang was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the emperor reviewed his replies and reflected on Jia's words; when Censor-in-Chief Jia Yan was dismissed, in summer, the fifth month, on yimao, Kong Guang was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙午，以光為丞相，復故國博山侯；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingwu, Guang was made chancellor and restored to his former state as Marquis of Boshan;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingwu, Kong Guang was appointed chancellor and restored to his former state as Marquis of Boshan;

sentences.zh: 又以汜鄉侯何武為御史大夫。

translations.literal: and Marquis of Sìxiang He Wu was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: and Marquis of Sìxiang He Wu was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 上乃知孔光前免非其罪，以過近臣毀短光者，曰：「傅嘉前為侍中，毀譖仁賢，誣訴大臣，令俊艾者久失其位，其免嘉為庶人，歸故郡。

translations.literal: The emperor then knew Kong Guang's earlier dismissal was not for his guilt; he punished close attendants who had defamed Guang, saying: "Fu Jia, formerly Attendant Within, slandered the humane and worthy and falsely accused great ministers, causing outstanding men long to lose their posts—dismiss Jia as a commoner and send him to his home commandery."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then knew Kong Guang's earlier dismissal was not for his guilt; he punished close attendants who had defamed Guang, saying: "Fu Jia, formerly Attendant Within, slandered the humane and worthy and falsely accused great ministers, keeping outstanding men long from office—dismiss Fu Jia to commoner rank and send him to his home commandery."

sentences.zh: 」八月，何武徙為前將軍。

translations.literal: " In the eighth month, He Wu was transferred to General of the Van.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eighth month, He Wu was transferred to General of the Van.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，光祿大夫彭宣為御史大夫。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Palace Chamberlain Peng Xuan was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Palace Chamberlain Peng Xuan was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 司隸鮑宣坐摧辱宰相，拒閉使者，無人臣禮，減死髡鉗。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Superintendent Bao Xuan sat for humiliating the chancellor and refusing and shutting out the envoy, lacking a minister's rites—his death sentence was reduced to shaving and shackles.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Superintendent Bao Xuan was convicted of humiliating the chancellor and refusing the envoy, lacking a minister's rites—his death sentence was reduced to shaving and shackles.

sentences.zh: 大司馬丁明素重王嘉，以其死而憐之；

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Ding Ming had always esteemed Wang Jia and pitied him for his death;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Ding Ming had always esteemed Wang Jia and pitied him for his death;

sentences.zh: 九月，乙卯，冊免明，使就第。

translations.literal: in the ninth month, on yimao, Ming was removed by patent and sent to his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: in the ninth month, on yimao, Ding Ming was removed by patent and sent to his mansion.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，壬午，以故定陶太傅、光祿大夫韋賞為大司馬、車騎將軍。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on renwu, the former Grand Tutor of Dingtao and Palace Chamberlain Wei Shang was made Grand Marshal and General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on renwu, the former Grand Tutor of Dingtao and Palace Chamberlain Wei Shang was appointed Grand Marshal and General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 己丑，賞卒。

translations.literal: On jichou, Shang died.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Wei Shang died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚子，以侍中、駙馬都尉董賢為大司馬、衛將軍，冊曰：「建爾於公，以為漢輔！

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengzi, Attendant Within and Commandant of Cavalry for the Emperor's Son-in-Law Dong Xian was made Grand Marshal and Defender-General; the patent read: "Establish you in the public sphere as Han's helper!
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengzi, Attendant Within and Commandant of Cavalry for the Emperor's Son-in-Law Dong Xian was appointed Grand Marshal and Defender-General; the patent read: "Establish you in the public sphere as Han's helper!

sentences.zh: 往悉爾心，匡正庶事，允執其中！

translations.literal: Go and exhaust your mind, rectify the multitude of affairs, and hold fast the mean!"
translations.idiomatic: Go and give your whole mind, rectify the multitude of affairs, and hold fast the mean!"

sentences.zh: 」是時賢年二十二，雖為三公，常給事中，領尚書，百官因賢奏事。

translations.literal: " At that time Xian was twenty-two; although one of the Three Ducal posts, he constantly served as Attendant Within, headed the Secretariat, and the hundred offices submitted affairs through Xian.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Dong Xian was twenty-two; although one of the Three Ducal posts, he constantly served as Attendant Within, headed the Secretariat, and the hundred offices submitted affairs through him.

sentences.zh: 以父衛尉恭不宜在卿位，徙為光祿大夫、秩中二千石；

translations.literal: Because his father Commandant of the Guard Gong was unfit for a ministerial post, he was transferred to Palace Chamberlain at the two-thousand-picul middle rank;
translations.idiomatic: Because his father Commandant of the Guard Gong was unfit for a ministerial post, he was transferred to Palace Chamberlain at the two-thousand-picul middle rank;

sentences.zh: 弟寬信代賢為駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: his younger brother Kuanxin replaced Xian as Commandant of Cavalry for the Emperor's Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother Kuanxin replaced Dong Xian as Commandant of Cavalry for the Emperor's Son-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 董氏親屬皆侍中、諸曹、奉朝請，寵在丁、傅之右矣。

translations.literal: The Dong clan's kin were all Attendants Within, bureau chiefs, and Court Assemblers—their favor surpassed the Ding and Fu clans.
translations.idiomatic: The Dong clan's kin were all Attendants Within, bureau chiefs, and court assemblers—their favor now surpassed the Ding and Fu clans.

sentences.zh: 初，丞相孔光為御史大夫，賢父恭為御史，事光。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chancellor Kong Guang was Censor-in-Chief, Xian's father Gong was a censor and served Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Chancellor Kong Guang was Censor-in-Chief, Dong Xian's father Gong was a censor and served under Guang.

sentences.zh: 及賢為大司馬，與光並為三公。

translations.literal: When Xian became Grand Marshal, he and Guang were together among the Three Ducal posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Xian became Grand Marshal, he and Kong Guang were together among the Three Ducal posts.

sentences.zh: 上故令賢私過光。

translations.literal: The emperor deliberately had Xian pay a private visit to Guang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deliberately had Dong Xian pay a private visit to Kong Guang.

sentences.zh: 光雅恭謹，知上欲尊寵賢。

translations.literal: Guang was by nature respectful and cautious and knew the emperor wished to honor and favor Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Guang was by nature respectful and cautious and knew the emperor wished to honor and favor Dong Xian.

sentences.zh: 及聞賢當來也，光警戒衣冠出門待，望見賢車乃卻入，賢至中門，光入閣，既下車，乃出，拜謁、送迎其謹，不敢以賓客鈞敵之禮。

translations.literal: When he heard Xian was coming, Guang dressed carefully and went out the gate to wait; seeing Xian's carriage he withdrew inside; when Xian reached the middle gate Guang entered the side chamber; only after Xian had alighted did he come out—bowing, paying respects, and escorting him with such caution that he did not dare use the guest-and-host equal courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Dong Xian was coming, Kong Guang dressed carefully and went out the gate to wait; seeing Dong Xian's carriage he withdrew inside; when Dong Xian reached the middle gate Kong Guang entered the side chamber; only after Dong Xian had alighted did he come out—bowing, paying respects, and escorting him with such caution that he did not dare treat him as an equal guest.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，喜，立拜光兩兄子為諫大夫、常侍。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it, was pleased, and immediately appointed Guang's two elder brothers' sons Remonstrance Grandee and Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it, was pleased, and immediately appointed Kong Guang's two elder brothers' sons Remonstrance Grandee and Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 賢由是權與人主侔矣。

translations.literal: Xian thereby came to wield power comparable to the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xian thereby came to wield power comparable to the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 是時，成帝外家王氏衰廢，唯平阿侯譚子去疾為侍中，弟閎為中常侍。

translations.literal: At that time the Wang clan of Emperor Cheng's maternal kin had declined; only Quji, son of Marquis of Ping'a Tan, was Attendant Within, and his younger brother Hong was Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Wang clan of Emperor Cheng's maternal kin had declined; only Quji, son of Marquis of Ping'a Tan, was Attendant Within, and his younger brother Hong was Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 閎妻父中郎將蕭鹹，前將軍望之子也，賢父恭慕之，欲為子寬信求鹹女為婦，使閎言之。

translations.literal: Hong's father-in-law Gentlemen-of-the-Household Xiao Xian, son of former General of the Van Wang, was admired by Xian's father Gong; Gong wished to seek Xian's daughter as wife for his son Kuanxin and had Hong speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's father-in-law Gentlemen-of-the-Household Xiao Xian, son of former General of the Van Wang, was admired by Dong Gong; Gong wished to seek Xiao Xian's daughter as wife for his son Kuanxin and had Hong speak of it.

sentences.zh: 鹹惶恐不敢當，私謂閎曰：「董公為大司馬，冊文言『允執其中』，此乃堯禪舜之文，非三公故事，長者見者莫不心懼。

translations.literal: Xian was fearful and did not dare accept; he privately told Hong: "Lord Dong as Grand Marshal—the patent's words 'hold fast the mean' are the text of Yao yielding to Shun; they are not the Three Ducal precedent; elders who see it are all inwardly afraid."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian was fearful and did not dare accept; he privately told Hong: "Lord Dong as Grand Marshal—the patent's words 'hold fast the mean' are the text of Yao yielding the throne to Shun; they are not the Three Ducal precedent; elders who see it are all inwardly afraid."

sentences.zh: 此豈家人子所能堪邪！

translations.literal: How can this be what a mere household son can bear!
translations.idiomatic: How can this be what a mere household son can bear!

sentences.zh: 」閎性有知略，聞鹹言，心亦悟；

translations.literal: " Hong by nature had knowledge and stratagem; hearing Xian's words, his mind also understood;
translations.idiomatic: " Hong by nature had judgment; hearing Xiao Xian's words, he also understood;

sentences.zh: 乃還報恭，深達鹹自謙薄之意。

translations.literal: he returned and reported to Gong, conveying in depth Xian's intent of self-deprecation and modesty.
translations.idiomatic: he returned and reported to Gong, conveying in depth Xiao Xian's intent of self-deprecation and modesty.

sentences.zh: 恭歎曰：「我家何用負天下，而為人所畏如是！

translations.literal: Gong sighed: "What need has my house to bear the empire, that we should be feared by others like this!
translations.idiomatic: Gong sighed: "What need has my house to bear the empire, that we should be feared by others like this!

sentences.zh: 」意不說。

translations.literal: " His mind was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " His mind was displeased.

sentences.zh: 後上置酒麒麟殿，賢父子、親屬宴飲，侍中、中常侍皆在側，上有酒所，從容視賢，笑曰：「吾欲法堯禪舜，何如？

translations.literal: Later the emperor set wine in the Qilin Hall; Xian, father and son, and kin feasted; Attendants Within and Palace Attendants-in-Ordinary were all at his side; when wine had taken effect he leisurely looked at Xian and said with a smile: "I wish to model Yao in yielding to Shun—how would that be?
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor set wine in the Qilin Hall; Dong Xian, father and son, and kin feasted; Attendants Within and Palace Attendants-in-Ordinary were all at his side; when wine had taken effect he leisurely looked at Dong Xian and said with a smile: "I wish to model Yao in yielding the throne to Shun—how would that be?

sentences.zh: 」王閎進曰：「天下乃高皇帝天下，非陛下之有也！

translations.literal: " Wang Hong advanced and said: "The empire is Emperor Gao's empire—not something Your Majesty possesses!
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Hong advanced and said: "The empire is Emperor Gao's empire—not something Your Majesty possesses!

sentences.zh: 陛下承宗廟，當傳子孫於亡窮，統業至重，天子亡戲言！

translations.literal: Your Majesty inherits the ancestral temple; you ought to transmit it to sons and grandsons without end—the unified enterprise is supremely weighty; the Son of Heaven has no jesting words!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty inherits the ancestral temple; you ought to transmit it to sons and grandsons without end—the unified enterprise is supremely weighty; the Son of Heaven has no jesting words!

sentences.zh: 」上默然不說，左右皆恐。

translations.literal: " The emperor was silent and displeased; those at his side were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was silent and displeased; those at his side were all afraid.

sentences.zh: 於是遣閎出歸郎署。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Hong out to return to his gentleman post.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he sent Hong out to return to his gentleman post.

sentences.zh: 久之，太皇太后為閎謝，復召閎還。

translations.literal: After a long while the Grand Empress Dowager apologized for Hong, and he was again summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while the Grand Empress Dowager apologized for Hong, and he was again summoned back.

sentences.zh: 閎遂上書諫曰：「臣聞王者立三公，法三光，居之者當得賢人。

translations.literal: Hong thereupon submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Your servant has heard that kings establish the Three Ducal posts, modeling the three luminaries—those who occupy them ought to obtain worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Hong thereupon submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Your servant has heard that kings establish the Three Ducal posts, modeling the three luminaries—those who occupy them ought to be worthy men.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：『鼎折足，覆公餗，』喻三公非其人也。

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'The cauldron's legs break; the lord's stew is overturned'—a metaphor that the Three Ducal posts are not held by the right men.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, 'The cauldron's legs break; the lord's stew is overturned'—a metaphor that the Three Ducal posts are not held by the right men.

sentences.zh: 昔孝文皇帝幸鄧通，不過中大夫；

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Xiaowen favored Deng Tong, yet advanced him no higher than Palace Grandee;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Wen favored Deng Tong, yet advanced him no higher than Palace Grandee;

sentences.zh: 武皇帝幸韓嫣，常賜而已，皆不在大位。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu favored Han Yan with frequent gifts only—neither held the great posts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu favored Han Yan with frequent gifts only—neither held the great posts.

sentences.zh: 今大司馬、衛將軍董賢，無功於漢朝，又無肺腑之連，復無名跡高行以矯世，升擢數年，列備鼎足，典衛禁兵，無功封爵，父子、兄弟橫蒙拔擢，賞賜空竭帑藏，萬民喧嘩，偶言道路，誠不當天心也！

translations.literal: Now Grand Marshal and Defender-General Dong Xian has no merit to the Han house, no bond of flesh and blood, and again no famous traces or lofty conduct to correct the age—yet within a few years of promotion he fills one leg of the tripod, commands the guard forbidden troops, received enfeoffment without merit; father, sons, and brothers recklessly received elevation; rewards and gifts emptied the treasury stores; the myriad people clamor and whisper along the roads—truly this does not accord with Heaven's mind!
translations.idiomatic: Now Grand Marshal and Defender-General Dong Xian has no merit to the Han house, no bond of flesh and blood, and again no famous deeds or lofty conduct to correct the age—yet within a few years of promotion he fills one leg of the tripod, commands the guard forbidden troops, received enfeoffment without merit; father, sons, and brothers recklessly received elevation; rewards and gifts emptied the treasury; the people clamor and whisper along the roads—truly this does not accord with Heaven's mind!

sentences.zh: 昔褒神蚖變化為人，實生褒姒，亂周國，恐陛下有過失之譏，賢有小人不知進退之禍，非所以垂法後世也！

translations.literal: Formerly the spirit serpent of Bao transformed into a man and in truth bore Bao Si, throwing the Zhou state into disorder—I fear Your Majesty will incur the reproach of fault, and Xian the misfortune of a petty man who does not know advance and retreat; this is not the means to hand down law to later ages!
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the spirit serpent of Bao transformed into a man and in truth bore Bao Si, throwing the Zhou state into disorder—I fear Your Majesty will incur the reproach of fault, and Dong Xian the misfortune of a petty man who does not know advance and retreat; this is not how to hand down law to later ages!

sentences.zh: 」上雖不從閎言，多其年少志強，亦不罪也。

translations.literal: " Although the emperor did not follow Hong's words, he admired his youth and strong will and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: " Although the emperor did not follow Hong's words, he admired his youth and strong will and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，匈奴單于及烏孫大昆彌伊秩靡皆來朝，漢以為榮。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Xiongnu chanyu and the Wusun Grand Kunmi Yizhimi both came to court; Han took it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the Xiongnu chanyu and the Wusun Grand Kunmi Yizhimi both came to court; the Han court took it as glory.

sentences.zh: 是時西域凡五十國，自譯長至將、相、侯、王皆佩漢印綬，凡三百七十六人；

translations.literal: At that time in the Western Regions there were fifty states in all; from interpreters-in-chief down to generals, chancellors, marquises, and kings—all wore Han seals and cords, three hundred seventy-six in all;
translations.idiomatic: At that time in the Western Regions there were fifty states in all; from interpreters-in-chief down to generals, chancellors, marquises, and kings—all wore Han seals and cords, three hundred seventy-six in all;

sentences.zh: 而康居、大月氏、安息、罽賓、烏弋之屬，皆以絕遠，不在數中，其來貢獻，則相與報，不督錄總領也。

translations.literal: but Kangju, Dayuezhi, Parthia, Jibin, Wuyi, and the like, all being extremely remote, were not counted among them; when they came to offer tribute, they were answered in turn and were not supervised, recorded, or overseen in total.
translations.idiomatic: but Kangju, Dayuezhi, Parthia, Jibin, Wuyi, and the like, all being extremely remote, were not counted among them; when they came to offer tribute, they were answered in turn and were not supervised or recorded in total.

sentences.zh: 自黃龍以來，單于每入朝，其賞賜錦繡、繒絮，輒加厚於前，以慰接之。

translations.literal: Since the Huanglong era, whenever the chanyu entered court, his rewards of brocade, embroidery, and silk floss were always thicker than before, to comfort and receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Huanglong era, whenever the chanyu entered court, his rewards of brocade, embroidery, and silk floss were always richer than before, to comfort and receive him.

sentences.zh: 單于宴見，群臣在前，單于怪董賢年少，以問譯。

translations.literal: At the chanyu's banquet audience, with the ministers before him, the chanyu wondered at Dong Xian's youth and asked the interpreter.
translations.idiomatic: At the chanyu's banquet audience, with the ministers before him, the chanyu wondered at Dong Xian's youth and asked the interpreter.

sentences.zh: 上令譯報曰：「大司馬年少，以大賢居位。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the interpreter to reply: "The Grand Marshal is young because great worthiness occupies the post."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the interpreter to reply: "The Grand Marshal is young because great worthiness occupies the post."

sentences.zh: 」單于乃起，拜賀漢得賢臣。

translations.literal: " The chanyu thereupon rose and bowed, congratulating Han on obtaining a worthy minister.
translations.idiomatic: " The chanyu thereupon rose and bowed, congratulating Han on obtaining a worthy minister.

sentences.zh: 是時上以大歲厭勝所在，捨單于上林苑蒲陶宮，告之以加敬於單于；

translations.literal: At that time, because the Grand Year star's conquering position lay there, the emperor lodged the chanyu at the Grape Palace in Shanglin Park and told him this showed added respect for the chanyu;
translations.idiomatic: At that time, because the Grand Year star's conquering position lay there, the emperor lodged the chanyu at the Grape Palace in Shanglin Park and told him this showed added respect for the chanyu;

sentences.zh: 單于知之，不悅。

translations.literal: the chanyu knew it and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: the chanyu knew it and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬辰晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the last day renchen of the cycle, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the last day renchen of the cycle, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 五月，甲子，正三公官分職。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jiazi, the Three Ducal offices were rectified and their duties divided.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiazi, the Three Ducal offices were rectified and their duties divided.

sentences.zh: 大司馬、衛將軍董賢為大司馬；

translations.literal: Grand Marshal and Defender-General Dong Xian was Grand Marshal;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal and Defender-General Dong Xian remained Grand Marshal;

sentences.zh: 丞相孔光為大司徒；

translations.literal: Chancellor Kong Guang was Grand Minister of the Masses;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Kong Guang became Grand Minister of the Masses;

sentences.zh: 御史大夫彭宣為大司空，封長平侯。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Peng Xuan was Grand Minister of Works and enfeoffed as Marquis of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Peng Xuan became Grand Minister of Works and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changping.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊午，帝崩於未央宮。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wuwu, the emperor collapsed at Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wuwu, the emperor died at Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝睹孝成之世祿去王室，及即位，屢誅大臣，欲強主威以則武、宣。

translations.literal: The emperor had seen that in Emperor Xiaocheng's age emoluments left the royal house; when he took the throne he repeatedly executed great ministers, wishing to strengthen the sovereign's authority to match Wu and Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had seen that in Emperor Cheng's reign emoluments left the royal house; when he took the throne he repeatedly executed great ministers, wishing to strengthen the sovereign's authority to match Wu and Xuan.

sentences.zh: 然而寵信讒諂，憎疾忠直，漢業由是遂衰。

translations.literal: Yet he favored and trusted slanderers and flatterers, hated and detested the loyal and upright—and the Han enterprise thereby declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he favored slanderers and flatterers, hated the loyal and upright—and the Han enterprise thereby declined.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后聞帝崩，即日駕之未央宮，收取璽綬。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager heard the emperor had collapsed; that very day she drove to Weiyang Palace and took the seals and cords.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager heard the emperor had died; that very day she drove to Weiyang Palace and took the seals and cords.

sentences.zh: 太后召大司馬賢，引見東箱，問以喪事調度。

translations.literal: The empress dowager summoned Grand Marshal Xian, received him in audience in the eastern side chamber, and questioned him on funeral arrangements and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager summoned Grand Marshal Dong Xian, received him in audience in the eastern side chamber, and questioned him on funeral arrangements and provisions.

sentences.zh: 賢內憂，不能對，免冠謝。

translations.literal: Xian was inwardly troubled and could not reply; he removed his cap and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xian was inwardly troubled and could not reply; he removed his cap and apologized.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「新都侯莽，前以大司馬奉送先帝大行，曉習故事，吾令莽佐君。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "Marquis of Xindu Mang, formerly as Grand Marshal escorted the late emperor's bier and is skilled in precedent—I order Mang to assist you."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said: "Marquis of Xindu Mang, formerly as Grand Marshal escorted the late emperor's bier and is skilled in precedent—I order Mang to assist you."

sentences.zh: 」賢頓首：「幸甚！

translations.literal: " Xian knocked his head on the ground: "Exceedingly fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: " Dong Xian knocked his head on the ground: "Exceedingly fortunate!

sentences.zh: 」太后遣使者馳召莽。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager sent a messenger post-haste to summon Mang.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager sent a messenger post-haste to summon Wang Mang.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書，諸發兵符節、百官奏事、中黃門、期門兵皆屬莽。

translations.literal: An edict to the Masters of Writing: all issuance of military tallies and seals, officials' memorials, Palace Attendants of the Yellow Gates, and Guard Corps troops were placed under Mang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to the Masters of Writing placed under Wang Mang all issuance of military tallies and seals, officials' memorials, Palace Attendants of the Yellow Gates, and Guard Corps troops.

sentences.zh: 莽以太后指，使尚書劾賢帝病不親醫藥，禁止賢不得入宮殿司馬中；

translations.literal: Mang, by the empress dowager's intent, had the Masters of Writing impeach Xian for not personally attending to the emperor's medicine when ill, and forbade Xian from entering the palace guard quarters;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang, acting on the empress dowager's intent, had the Masters of Writing impeach Dong Xian for failing to attend personally to the emperor's medicine during his illness, and forbade Xian from entering the palace guard quarters;

sentences.zh: 賢不知所為，詣闕免冠徒跣謝。

translations.literal: Xian did not know what to do and went to the palace gate bareheaded and barefoot to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Xian did not know what to do and went to the palace gate bareheaded and barefoot to apologize.

sentences.zh: 己未，莽使謁者以太后詔即闕下冊賢曰：「賢年少，未更事理，為大司馬，不合眾心，其收大司馬印綬，罷歸第！

translations.literal: On jiwei, Mang had an usher read the empress dowager's edict at the gate to dismiss Xian, saying: "Xian is young and has not yet experienced affairs; as Grand Marshal he does not accord with popular hearts—let him surrender the Grand Marshal's seal and cord and retire to his residence!
